questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

schema.name: SendUserFile
schema.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Fabric is its own product, so no existing key fits and new keys are warranted. Make sure both keys are in MaesterTaxonomy.psd1, with 'export-and-sharing' listed under the 'fabric' product, or the unit tests will fail.
- CIS.M365.9.1.2: UserImpact 'Medium' is defensible because users outside the scoped groups lose the ability to invite guests while sharing. 'Low' could be argued if few users invite guests through Fabric.

The control only limits discovery of content through browsing by guests, it needs a guest account to be compromised first, and direct permissions are unaffected. Medium could also be argued, and the rubric picks the lower level when two fit. CIS.M365.9.1.1 checks a different setting, whether guests can access Fabric at all, so its Medium is not a mismatch.
- CIS.M365.9.1.3: T1213 fits the data-collection risk that the description names.
- CIS.M365.9.1.4: The supplied taxonomy does not list the product `fabric` or the feature `export-and-sharing`. Related tests in the repository already use both keys, so the taxonomy file most likely has them. Confirm that `MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` defines both, or add them in this pull request; the unit tests will fail otherwise.
- CIS.M365.9.1.4: Severity `Medium` is defensible. A public embed code exposes data to the internet without sign-in, but someone inside the organization must first publish a report, and the exposure is limited to the reports published.
- CIS.M365.9.1.4: T1567 is consistent with CIS.M365.9.1.8 (external sharing of semantic models). Publish to web gives an unauthenticated web channel out of the tenant.
- CIS.M365.9.1.5: Add a `fabric` (Microsoft Fabric) product with a `tenant-settings` feature to powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1 in this pull request. The remediation sends the admin to Fabric Admin portal > Tenant settings, so these keys fit once they exist.
- CIS.M365.9.1.5: Area `infrastructure` is defensible because this is a tenant-wide platform setting. `data-protection` would also be arguable if the concern is data leaving the tenant through script visuals.
- CIS.M365.9.1.5: Severity `Medium` is defensible. Script visuals run in Microsoft's sandbox, and abusing them requires a user who can author reports, so `Low` would also be arguable.
- CIS.M365.9.1.5: Mitre T1059 is acceptable as the parent technique. R has no sub-technique, so listing T1059 rather than T1059.006 alone is reasonable.
- CIS.M365.9.1.5: Service = 'Azure' looks off for a Fabric tenant setting. Consider whether a Fabric/Power BI service value is more accurate.
- CIS.M365.9.1.6: Product 'fabric' and the feature 'information-protection' under it are not in the taxonomy provided. In the taxonomy, 'information-protection' is a Purview feature. The fix is made in the Fabric admin portal, so a new 'fabric' product is warranted. Add it to MaesterTaxonomy.psd1 in this pull request, with a feature list that includes the information protection tenant settings, or the unit tests will fail.
- CIS.M365.9.1.6: Consider RelatedProduct = 'purview'. The labels are created and published in Purview, and remediation step 1 depends on that.
- CIS.M365.9.1.6: ImplementationCost Medium is defensible. The toggle is one setting, but step 1 depends on labels being published and licensing being in place, which usually needs the Purview team.
- CIS.M365.9.1.6: Mitre None is acceptable because the description names no attacker behaviour. Labels can support defences against exfiltration, such as T1567, if the description explains how.
- CIS.M365.9.1.7: Product 'fabric' and feature 'export-and-sharing' are not in the taxonomy provided for this review. No existing product fits Microsoft Fabric tenant settings, so new keys are warranted. Make sure MaesterTaxonomy.psd1 adds them in this pull request, or the unit tests will fail.

- CIS.M365.9.1.7: Severity 'Low' is defensible: exposure is limited to internal users and to content someone chose to share. 'Medium' would also be arguable.
- CIS.M365.9.1.7: Mitre 'None' is acceptable because the description frames the risk as accidental internal disclosure. T1213 (Data from Information Repositories) is a plausible addition if the description is extended to name an insider or a compromised account browsing broadly shared content.
- CIS.M365.9.1.8: The taxonomy supplied for this review has no `fabric` product and no `export-and-sharing` feature. Existing tests CIS.M365.9.1.1 to 9.1.7 already use them, so the repository taxonomy probably has them. Confirm that `MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` defines both keys and pairs `export-and-sharing` with `fabric`.
- CIS.M365.9.1.8: Mitre: T1537 (Transfer Data to Cloud Account) may fit in-place sharing of semantic models with another tenant's users better than, or alongside, T1567. T1567 is defensible because the Markdown names a path for data to leave the organization.
- CIS.M365.9.1.8: Severity Medium fits. Misuse needs a signed-in user who deliberately shares, and the exposure is limited to one workload (semantic models). The related tests in this family are a different check (public publishing, CIS.M365.9.1.4) but have the same rating.
- CIS.M365.9.1.8: No related test checks the same setting (EnableDatasetInPlaceSharing), so no cross-suite consistency findings apply.
- CIS.M365.9.1.8: `Service = 'Azure'` looks unusual for a Fabric tenant setting. It is not a rubric attribute, but check that it is intended.
- CIS.M365.9.1.9: Product 'fabric' and Feature 'developer-settings' are not in the supplied taxonomy, and no existing product covers Microsoft Fabric, so new keys are warranted. Add both to MaesterTaxonomy.psd1 in this pull request if they are not already there; the related tests suggest the repository may already have them.
- CIS.M365.9.1.9: Area 'authentication' fits: the control replaces shared resource keys with identity-based authentication.
- CIS.M365.9.1.9: UserImpact 'Medium' is defensible because clients and dashboards that push data with resource keys stop updating. If only integration owners are affected, 'Low' could also be argued.
- CIS.M365.9.1.9: ImplementationCost 'Medium' fits: the setting is a single toggle, but clients that still use resource keys must first be updated, which needs coordination with their owners.
- CIS.M365.9.1.9: Mitre 'None' is accepted because the description does not name attacker behaviour. A technique for misuse of leaked shared keys, such as T1550.001 or T1552, could be considered if the Markdown is expanded to explain that threat.
- CIS.M365.9.1.9: The related tests (CIS.M365.9.1.10, 9.1.11 and 9.1.12) check service principal API access, not resource-key authentication, so they are not the same check and were not compared.

Change the value, or explain in the pull request why the declared value fits the rubric. A maintainer can overrule this check with the `attribute-review-override` label.

content.text:
I posted the retest request on [#2556](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2556#issuecomment-6467587361).

**CI on `7fdc2df2e`:** build validation passes on ubuntu, windows and macOS, and so does every other check except **attribute-review**.

**Why attribute-review fails:** 11 of the 12 tests pass. It fails `CIS.M365.9.1.5` on its `Product = 'fabric'` and `Feature = 'tenant-settings'` values, saying neither is in the taxonomy. Both are in the PR's `MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`, but the review script reads the taxonomy from `main` on purpose (`Invoke-MtAttributeReview.ps1:376`, the "trusted root"), so the bot can't see keys that a PR adds.

The other 11 tests got the same "not in the taxonomy" note but passed anyway. The unit test that checks every value against the PR's own taxonomy passes. So this failure is the case the `attribute-review-override` label exists for.

The bot also suggested some values that aren't failures. I'd leave them for Jeremy:
- **`Service = 'Azure'` looks odd for these checks.** We keep it on purpose, because the token comes from the Azure connection.
- **9.1.6 could add `RelatedProduct = 'purview'`.** It's a reasonable suggestion; the sensitivity labels it relies on are managed in Purview.

content.content:
"The author pushed" includes co-authors and agents committing for the author. When the PR's
author is a maintainer, their own pushes count the same way. A merge commit from `main` on its
own is not a response; look for a commit that changes the files the review was about.

Issues. Take the first rule that matches.

| Label | When |
| --- | --- |
| `status: awaiting confirmation` | A PR that closes it has merged, or a maintainer said the fix shipped and is waiting for the reporter. Suggest closing it in the report. |
| `status: blocked` | It waits on another open item, an unreleased feature, or an upstream product or module fix. |
| `status: needs info` | A maintainer's latest comment asks the reporter a question and the reporter has not answered. |
| `status: needs decision` | A maintainer has to decide whether or how to do it, including a reporter asking a maintainer to choose (a severity, a default, an approach). |
| `status: in progress` | An open PR closes it (a closing keyword such as "fixes #N", or the Development sidebar), or it has an assignee and activity in the last 90 days. A mention such as "related to #N" or "tracked in #N" does not count. |
| `status: accepted` | A maintainer opened it, labelled it, confirmed the bug or agreed to the feature, and nobody has started it. |
| `status: needs triage` | No maintainer has engaged yet, **or** the reporter answered a maintainer's question and it is the maintainers' turn again. |

A maintainer opening, labelling or assigning an issue counts as engaging with it. Skip pinned
issues (such as the MT test ID reservation thread, #697): they are permanent and take no status.

Discussions. Take the first rule that matches; a discussion that matches none gets no status.

# Manage Azure subscription policies - Microsoft Cost Management | Microsoft Learn

This article helps you to configure Azure subscription policies to control the movement of Azure subscriptions from and into directories. The default behavior of these two policies is set to **Allow no users (recommended)** to help protect tenants from unauthorized subscription transfers. Global administrators can change these settings to **Allow all users** if needed. Note that the setting of **Allow all users** allows all authorized users, including authorized guest users on a subscription, to be able to transfer them. It does not mean all users in a directory.

Important

To improve tenant security, on May 1st, 2026, Microsoft updated the default behavior for subscription transfer policies. Subscriptions can no longer be transferred in to or out of your directory unless a global administrator explicitly allows it.

If your organization previously set an explicit policy, that choice continues to be respected — no action is needed.

If your organization never configured these policies and your workflows rely on users being able to move subscriptions in or out of your tenant, **those workflows will break as a result of this change**. To restore the previous behavior, a global administrator can update either policy to **Allow all users**.

## Prerequisites

- Only directory [global administrators](../../active-directory/roles/permissions-reference#global-administrator) with direct role assignment can edit subscription policies. Before editing subscription policies, the global administrator must [Elevate access to manage all Azure subscriptions and management groups](../../role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin). Then they can edit subscription policies.
- All other users can only read the current policy setting.
- Subscriptions transferred into or out of a directory must remain associated with a Billing Tenant to ensure billing occurs correctly.

## Available subscription policy settings

Use the following policy settings to control the movement of Azure subscriptions from and into directories.

### Subscriptions leaving a Microsoft Entra ID directory

The policy allows or stops users from moving subscriptions out of the current directory. Subscription owners can transfer subscriptions to another directory where they're a member, using either the Azure portal or APIs. Global administrators use this setting to allow or block these transfers for all directory users. This policy applies to all authorized users, including authorized guest users in your directory.

- **Allow no users (recommended)** — Blocks all subscription transfers out of your directory. This is the default.
- **Allow all users** — Permits authorized users to transfer subscriptions out of your directory.

### Subscriptions entering a Microsoft Entra ID directory

This policy controls whether users from other directories can move subscriptions into your directory. Subscription owners who are members of your directory can transfer subscriptions in using the Azure portal or APIs. Global administrators use this setting to allow or block these transfers. This policy applies to all authorized users, including authorized guest users in your directory.

- **Allow no users (recommended)** — Blocks all subscription transfers into your directory. This is the default.
- **Allow all users** — Permits authorized users to transfer subscriptions into your directory.

### Exempted Users

For governance reasons, global administrators can block all subscription directory moves - in to or out of the current directory. However they might want to allow specific users to do both operations. For both situations, they can configure a list of exempted users that allows these users to bypass all the policy settings that apply to everyone else.

#### Important note

Authorized users (including guest users) in your directory can create Azure subscriptions in another directory where they have billing permissions and then transfer those subscriptions into your Entra ID directory. The default policy settings (**Allow no users**) help protect against this scenario. If your organization has changed either policy to **Allow all users**, be aware of this risk and consider reverting to the recommended default:

- Subscriptions leaving Entra ID directory should be set to **Allow no users (recommended)**.
- Subscriptions entering Entra ID directory should be set to **Allow no users (recommended)**.

## Setting subscription policy

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
2. Navigate to **Subscriptions**. **Manage Policies** is shown on the command bar. [![Screenshot of the Azure Subscriptions blade with the Manage Policies button highlighted.](media/manage-azure-subscription-policy/subscription-blade-manage-policies.png)](media/manage-azure-subscription-policy/subscription-blade-manage-policies.png#lightbox)
3. Select **Manage Policies** to view details about the current subscription policies set for the directory. A global administrator with [elevated permissions](../../role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin) can make edits to the settings including adding or removing exempted users.[![Screenshot of the Manage Policies pane showing subscription policy details.](media/manage-azure-subscription-policy/2026-04-15-14-52-13.png)](media/manage-azure-subscription-policy/2026-04-15-14-52-13.png#lightbox)
4. Select **Save changes** at the bottom to save changes. The changes are effective immediately.

## Read subscription policy

Non-global administrators can still navigate to the subscription policy area to view the directory's policy settings. They can't make any edits. They can't see the list of exempted users for privacy reasons. They can view their global administrators to submit requests for policy changes, as long as the directory settings allow them to.

content.text: The user hasn't heard from you in a while — say in a few words what you're doing, then continue.

**#2556:** the `attribute-review-override` label is on, with a [one-line reason](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2556#issuecomment-6467819645). The attribute-review check now shows as skipped.

**#2472 (MT.1227, subscriptions blocked from leaving the tenant):** Oppedijk hasn't answered your 22 Oct review; the only pushes since are merges from `main`. Build validation on ubuntu fails for the reasons that review gave: missing final newline, the `en-us` link, and stale `selection.json` and `test-builder.json`.

**One of your review points was wrong.** Point 3 said Microsoft's default is "Allow everyone". [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/manage-azure-subscription-policy) says that on 1 May 2026 the default became **"Allow no users"**, which blocks transfers. So the `.md` sentence that the block is on by default is correct.

That raises a question about the `TenantPolicyNotFound` branch. If a tenant that never set a policy gets that response, its transfers are blocked by default, yet the test reports a fail. Oppedijk says Microsoft now returns a default policy, so this branch may never run. Either way, I'd make it pass with a note rather than fail.

**What's still open from your review:**
- **A 403 is no longer reported as a fail, but it still isn't skipped.** `main` now has `Invoke-MtAzureRequest` return `$null` on 401/403, so a 403 lands in the null branch. That branch returns `$false` with `-Investigate`; it should skip and return `$null`.
- **The required role is wrong in the docs.** The remediation names Subscription Policy Contributor or Owner. Only a directly assigned Global Administrator who has elevated access can edit the policy, and any user can read it.
- **Attributes, which you said you'd decide.** I'd keep the new `subscriptions` feature, next to `management-groups`. I'd change `Area` to `infrastructure`, because the rubric names subscriptions there explicitly.
- **Minor:** the `.LINK` on the helper and the AC-3 vs AC-4 control mapping.

All of this is small and mechanical, and the PR has been waiting on Oppedijk for 6 days.

The recommendation number depends on the CIS Azure Foundations version:

- **v2.1.0:** Item 1.24, now deprecated. This audit has been deprecated and will be removed in a future update.
- **v3.0.0:** Item 2.25 (Level 2). The source lists it as "2.25 Ensure That 'Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant' and 'Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant' Is Set To 'Permit no one'" (index 4-1).

content.text:
It isn't in the CIS **Microsoft 365** benchmark. Your v7.0.0 PDF doesn't mention the subscription transfer policy anywhere.

It is in the CIS **Azure** Foundations benchmark (sources: [Tenable v4.0.0 audit](https://www.tenable.com/audits/items/CIS_Microsoft_Azure_Foundations_v4.0.0_L2.audit:1d8f72558170c6d5638e34d6e6c2f6f8), [Turbot CIS v5.0 5.25](https://hub.guardrails.turbot.com/mods/azure/controls/azure-cisv5-0/r0525)):

| CIS Azure version | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| v3.0.0 | 2.25 (Level 2) |
| v4.0.0 | 6.25 (Level 2) |
| v5.0.0 | 5.25 (Identity Services, Level 2) |

All three word it as "Ensure that 'Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant' **and** 'Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant' is set to 'Permit no one'".

For #2472, that means:
- **MT.1227 is the right ID.** Maester has no CIS Azure framework file (only `cis-m365` and `cis-github`), so there's no `cis-azure:5.25` for the check to map to. It belongs in `tests/maester/azure/` as an MT check, as Oppedijk wrote it.
- **It covers only half the CIS control.** It checks `blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant`. CIS also requires `blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant`, which comes back in the same policy response. Microsoft's Learn page also recommends blocking both directions, because an insider can create a subscription in a tenant they control and move it in. If we fix this ourselves, I'd add that check too, as a second test or as part of this one.
- **The CIS text is out of date.** It says the default is "Allow everyone". Microsoft changed it to "Allow no users" on 1 May 2026, which is probably where your 22 Oct review point came from.

The search didn't turn up a CIS primary source, so these findings come from vendor documentation and tool listings. They point to **v6.0.0** as the newest version, but the sources conflict on the timeline.

- **v6.0.0:** Trend Vision One's February 3, 2026 release notes say it added CIS Azure Foundations Benchmark v6.0.0 and deprecated v4.1.0. A PowerShell module from the same period also audits Azure subscriptions against the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v6.0.0.
- **v5.0.0:** A Trend Vision One note dated March 25, 2026 lists CIS Azure Foundations Benchmark v5.0.0 as the update. That date is later than the v6.0.0 note, so the ordering is unclear. Another module describes 155 CIS controls (93 Automated + 62 Manual) under v5.0.0.
- **Earlier versions:** In December 2025, Trend Cloud One's release notes added v4.0.0 and deprecated the CIS Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.1.0 for removal on February 8 2026.

My reading is that v6.0.0 is the most recent version, but the vendor notes don't agree on the ordering. For authoritative confirmation, check CIS's own benchmark page or its download portal.

No. v7.0.0 is the CIS **Microsoft 365** benchmark, the PDF already in your Downloads. The latest **Azure** Foundations benchmark is **v6.0.0**, according to [CIS's own benchmark page](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/azure). Vendor notes such as [Trend Vision One's v6 release note](https://docs.trendmicro.com/en-us/documentation/article/trend-vision-one-cis-azure-foundations-benchmark-6) say the same.

You'll need to download it yourself. CIS gives the PDFs away free for non-commercial use, but the download goes through a form at [learn.cisecurity.org/benchmarks](https://learn.cisecurity.org/benchmarks) that asks for your name and email, and I don't fill in personal details or register accounts for you.

Once it's in Downloads, I'll extract the text the same way I did for the M365 PDF. Then I'll confirm the v6.0.0 recommendation number for the subscription policy (5.25 in v5.0.0), its audit and remediation steps, and whether it still says the default is "Allow everyone".

● ● ●

6.8 Define and Maintain Role-Based Access Control
Define and maintain role-based access control, through determining and
documenting the access rights necessary for each role within the enterprise to
successfully carry out its assigned duties. Perform access control reviews of
enterprise assets to validate that all privileges are authorized, on a recurring
schedule at a minimum annually, or more frequently.
●
v7
14.6 Protect Information through Access Control Lists
Protect all information stored on systems with file system, network share, claims,
application, or database specific access control lists. These controls will enforce the
principle that only authorized individuals should have access to the information
based on their need to access the information as a part of their responsibilities.

5.6 Ensure that 'Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant' and
'Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant' is set to 'Permit no
one' (Manual)
Profile Applicability:
• Level 2
Description:
Users who are set as subscription owners are able to make administrative changes to
the subscriptions and move them into and out of Microsoft Entra ID.
Rationale:
Permissions to move subscriptions in and out of a Microsoft Entra tenant must only be

content.text:
`CIS_Microsoft_Azure_Foundations_Benchmark_v6.0.0.pdf` is in Downloads; its cover says "V6.0.0 - 04-19-2026". In v6.0.0 the control has moved to **5.6** (it was 5.25 in v5.0.0). It's on printed pages 111–112.

**5.6: Ensure that 'Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant' and 'Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant' is set to 'Permit no one'** (Level 2, Manual)
- **Audit:** in the Azure portal, open Subscriptions, then Manage Policies, and check that both settings are "Permit no one".
- **Remediation:** set both settings to "Permit no one" in the same place, then save.
- **Default value:** CIS still says both are "Allow everyone (default)". That's out of date: Microsoft changed the default to "Allow no users" on 1 May 2026, a couple of weeks after this release.
- **References:** the Microsoft Learn subscription policy page, "How subscriptions are associated with a directory", and MCSB IM-2.

What this means for #2472:
- **It checks only half the control.** The recommendation covers both directions, but MT.1227 only checks `blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant`. `blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant` comes back in the same API response, so adding it is a few lines.
- **It stays an MT test.** Maester has no `cis-azure` framework file, so there's nothing to map 5.6 to. The test can say in its Markdown that it lines up with CIS Azure 5.6.

function Test-MtSubscriptionTransferBlocked {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks whether Azure subscriptions are blocked from leaving and entering the tenant.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Checks the tenant-level Azure subscription policy. Allowing subscriptions to leave
    the tenant can let a privileged user transfer their resources to an external tenant.
    Allowing subscriptions to enter the tenant can let a user bring in a subscription
    they control from another tenant.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MT.1227',
        Title              = 'Subscriptions should be blocked from leaving and entering the tenant',
        Product            = 'azure',
        Feature            = 'subscriptions',
        Area               = 'infrastructure',
        ResourceType       = 'Tenant',
        Severity           = 'Medium',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = 'T1537',
        Control            = 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-4',
        Service            = 'Azure',
        Author             = 'Oppedijk',
        Contributor        = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $policy = Get-MtAzureSubscriptionPolicy

    if ($null -eq $policy) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotAuthorized
        return $null
    }

    $policyNotFound = $policy.code -eq 'TenantPolicyNotFound' -or
        $policy.error.code -eq 'TenantPolicyNotFound'

    if ($policyNotFound) {
        # Since 1 May 2026 a tenant without an explicit policy blocks transfers in both directions.
        $testResultMarkdown = 'Well done. No tenant subscription policy is set, so the Microsoft default blocks subscriptions from leaving and entering the tenant.'
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
        return $true
    }

    if ($policy.error) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error -SkippedError $policy.error.message
        return $null
    }

    $blockLeaving = $policy.properties.blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant -eq $true
    $blockEntering = $policy.properties.blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant -eq $true
    $testResult = $blockLeaving -and $blockEntering

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = 'Well done. The tenant subscription policy blocks subscriptions from leaving and entering the tenant.'
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The tenant subscription policy allows subscriptions to move into or out of the tenant.`n`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Setting | Value |`n| --- | --- |`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant | $(if ($blockLeaving) { 'Permit no one ✅' } else { 'Allow everyone ❌' }) |`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant | $(if ($blockEntering) { 'Permit no one ✅' } else { 'Allow everyone ❌' }) |"
    }

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

function Test-MtSubscriptionTransferBlocked {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks whether Azure subscriptions are blocked from leaving and entering the tenant.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Checks the tenant-level Azure subscription policy. Allowing subscriptions to leave
    the tenant can let a privileged user transfer their resources to an external tenant.
    Allowing subscriptions to enter the tenant can let a user bring in a subscription
    they control from another tenant.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MT.1227',
        Title              = 'Subscriptions should be blocked from leaving and entering the tenant',
        Product            = 'azure',
        Feature            = 'subscriptions',
        Area               = 'infrastructure',
        ResourceType       = 'Tenant',
        Severity           = 'Medium',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = 'T1537',
        Control            = 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-4',
        Service            = 'Azure',
        Author             = 'Oppedijk',
        Contributor        = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $policy = Get-MtAzureSubscriptionPolicy

    if ($null -eq $policy) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotAuthorized
        return $null
    }

    $errorCode = if ($policy.error) { $policy.error.code } else { $policy.code }

    if ($errorCode -eq 'TenantPolicyNotFound') {
        # Since 1 May 2026 a tenant without an explicit policy blocks transfers in both directions.
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'Well done. No tenant subscription policy is set, so the Microsoft default blocks subscriptions from leaving and entering the tenant.'
        return $true
    }

    if ($errorCode) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error -SkippedError ($policy | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5)
        return $null
    }

    $blockLeaving = $policy.properties.blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant -eq $true
    $blockEntering = $policy.properties.blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant -eq $true
    $testResult = $blockLeaving -and $blockEntering

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = 'Well done. The tenant subscription policy blocks subscriptions from leaving and entering the tenant.'
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The tenant subscription policy allows subscriptions to move into or out of the tenant.`n`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Setting | Value |`n| --- | --- |`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant | $(if ($blockLeaving) { '✅ Permit no one' } else { '❌ Allow everyone' }) |`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant | $(if ($blockEntering) { '✅ Permit no one' } else { '❌ Allow everyone' }) |"
    }

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

﻿function Test-MtSubscriptionLeavingTenantBlocked {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks whether Azure subscriptions are blocked from leaving the tenant.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Checks the tenant-level Azure subscription policy. Allowing subscriptions to leave
    the tenant can let a privileged user transfer their resources to an external tenant.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MT.1227',
        Title              = 'Subscriptions should be blocked from leaving the tenant',
        Product            = 'azure',
        Feature            = 'subscriptions',
        Area               = 'access-control',
        ResourceType       = 'Tenant',
        Severity           = 'Medium',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = 'T1537',
        Control            = 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-3',
        Service            = 'Azure',
        Author             = 'Oppedijk'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $policy = Get-MtAzureSubscriptionPolicy

    if($null -eq $policy) {
        $testResult = $false
        $testResultMarkdown = 'No tenant subscription policy was returned. This check cannot determine the effective transfer-blocking behavior from an absent policy. Verify the tenant''s effective settings and configure an explicit policy if needed.'
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown -Investigate
        return $testResult
    }

    $policyNotFound = $policy.code -eq 'TenantPolicyNotFound' -or
        $policy.error.code -eq 'TenantPolicyNotFound'

    if ($policyNotFound) {
        $testResult = $false
        $testResultMarkdown = 'No tenant subscription policy is assigned. Enable the policy to prevent subscriptions from leaving the tenant.'
    } else {
        $testResult = $policy.properties.blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant -eq $true

        if ($testResult) {
            $testResultMarkdown = 'Well done. The tenant subscription policy blocks subscriptions from leaving the tenant without authorization.'
        } else {
            $testResultMarkdown = 'The tenant subscription policy does not block subscriptions from leaving the tenant. Enable blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant to prevent unauthorized transfers.'
        }
    }

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

input.content:
Subscriptions should be blocked from leaving and entering the tenant.

The tenant subscription policy controls whether subscription owners can move a subscription out of the tenant or bring one in from another tenant. Allowing subscriptions to leave can let a privileged user transfer a subscription and its resources to an external tenant. Allowing subscriptions to enter can let a user bring in a subscription they control, together with its resources and role assignments.

Since 1 May 2026 Microsoft blocks both directions by default for tenants that never set a policy. A tenant that set **Allow everyone** before then keeps that setting. This check also covers CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v6.0.0 recommendation 5.6.

#### Remediation action

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com) as a Global Administrator with a direct role assignment, and [elevate access](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin) to manage all Azure subscriptions. Other users can read the policy but not change it.
2. Go to **Subscriptions** and select **Manage Policies**.
3. Set **Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant** and **Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant** to **Permit no one**.
4. If specific users must still move subscriptions, add them to **Exempted Users**.
5. Select **Save changes**.

#### Related links

- [Manage Azure subscription policies - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/manage-azure-subscription-policy)
- [Azure portal - Subscriptions](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Billing/SubscriptionsBladeV2)

Subscriptions should be blocked from leaving the tenant.

Allowing subscriptions to leave the tenant without restriction can let a privileged user transfer a subscription and its resources to an external tenant. The tenant subscription policy can require explicit authorization before a subscription is moved. The Microsoft default is that when there is no policy, the block is enabled by default.

#### Remediation action

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com) as a user with the **Subscription Policy Contributor** or **Owner** role at the tenant scope. A directly assigned Global Admin can do this.
2. Open a PowerShell Cloud Shell session and enable the policy:

```powershell
$token = (Get-AzAccessToken).Token
$body = @{ blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant = $true } | ConvertTo-Json
Invoke-RestMethod -Method PUT -Uri "https://management.azure.com/providers/Microsoft.Subscription/policies/default?api-version=2021-10-01" -Authentication Bearer -Token $token -Body $body
```

3. Confirm `properties.blockSubscriptionsLeavingTenant` is `true` in the policy response.

#### Related links

- [Manage Azure subscription policies - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/manage-azure-subscription-policy)
- [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com)

input.content:
Thanks @Oppedijk. I've pushed the fixes from my review to your branch, plus a correction to my own review:

- **Microsoft's default has changed.** In point 3 I said the default is "Allow everyone". That was true until 1 May 2026, when Microsoft [changed it to "Allow no users"](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/manage-azure-subscription-policy) for tenants that never set a policy. So your sentence about the default was right. A `TenantPolicyNotFound` response now passes, with a note that the default blocks transfers.
- **The check covers both directions.** CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations v6.0.0 recommendation 5.6 asks for both "Subscription leaving" and "Subscription entering" to be set to "Permit no one", and Microsoft recommends the same. `blockSubscriptionsIntoTenant` comes back in the same response, so the check now requires both. The title is now "Subscriptions should be blocked from leaving and entering the tenant", and the function is renamed to `Test-MtSubscriptionTransferBlocked`. When the check fails, the result shows a table with both settings.
- **An unreadable policy is skipped.** `Invoke-MtAzureRequest` now returns `$null` on 401/403, and that case is skipped as `NotAuthorized` instead of failing. Any other error response is skipped as `Error`.
- **Attributes.** I kept your `subscriptions` feature. `Area` is now `infrastructure`, because the rubric lists subscriptions there. `Control` is now AC-4.
- **Docs.** The remediation now names the right role: a directly assigned Global Administrator who has elevated access, since other users can only read the policy. It uses the portal's Manage Policies steps instead of a PUT, because a PUT also replaces the exempted users. I removed `en-us` from the links.
- **CI.** I added the final newlines, regenerated `selection.json` and `test-builder.json`, and merged `main`.

If you can, please run it once against your tenant before we merge:

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -TestId 'MT.1227'
```
